bio: Zuzana Čániová completed her MD at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad in 2003 and defended her PhD on quantitative sensory testing in diabetic neuropathy at the same institution in 2010. Her group investigates the relationship between somatosensory phenotypes—mapped using standardised quantitative sensory testing batteries—and small-fibre density assessed from skin punch biopsies in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Secondary interests include autonomic involvement and the longitudinal trajectory of sensory loss. She teaches neurology and clinical neurophysiology at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The group operates within the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina neurology service and uses an in-house QST setup calibrated to the German Research Network on Neuropathic Pain protocol, a confocal microscopy platform for PGP 9.5-immunostained biopsy sections, and sudomotor function testing equipment.

Her group regularly uses photogrammetric scanning equipment and GIS platforms available through the faculty laboratory for spatial analysis.

The group makes regular use of learning management system log data, think-aloud protocols, and validated metacognitive questionnaires. He teaches courses in instructional design and media in education.
